notes: Both boards are Arduino Nano Every. A4 is SDA and A5 is SCL on both. SDA goes to SDA and SCL to SCL, as in the image.

The image shows the SDA and SCL lines joined between the boards, each with a 4.7k pull-up to the reader's 3V pin, and GND joined between the boards. It does not show the breadboards, so I arranged them to fit the parts list of 2 mini breadboards and 10 jumper wires. That arrangement is an assumption.

bb1 holds the pull-ups. Column 5 top is the SDA strip, column 8 top is the SCL strip, the top positive rail (tp) is 3V and the top negative rail (tn) is GND. The reader's A4, A5, 3V3 and GND wires plug into bb1.

bb2 holds the writer's connections. Its SDA strip (5t), SCL strip (8t) and GND rail (tn) are linked to the same nets on bb1 by three jumper wires (wire8, wire7, wire9). The writer's A4, A5 and GND wires plug into bb2.
The 3V rail is connected only to the reader's 3V pin, as in the image. The writer is powered by USB, so nothing connects to its 3V pin.
I changed wire9's colour from red (step 1) to brown, because it carries GND. Each pull-up resistor goes from its signal strip to the 3V rail (r1 for SCL, r2 for SDA).
Each USB cable joins its board's USB port. The far end goes to the computer, which is not a part in the graph.
